title: When is it OK to complain? ☝️😠 | Practise your listening skills with Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hi Neil. How are you doing?
I'm very well, thank you Georgie. How are you?
sentences.ko: 아주 잘 지내, 고마워 조지. 너는?

sentences.en: I'm very well too.
Neil, in this episode of Real Easy English we're talking about complaining – that is when you say something is wrong, or you have a problem and you want to tell someone about it.
sentences.ko: 닐, 이번 Real Easy English에서는 불평(complaining)에 대해 이야기할 거야. 뭔가 잘못됐다고 말하거나, 문제가 있어서 누군가에게 그걸 알리고 싶을 때 말이야.

sentences.en: Yes. And people should remember that they can get a free worksheet for this podcast at bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: 맞아. 그리고 이 팟캐스트의 무료 워크시트를 bbclearningenglish.com에서 받을 수 있다는 걸 기억해 주세요.

sentences.en: I know that you have a recent experience with this, don't you?
sentences.ko: 너 최근에 이런 일을 겪었지, 그렇지?

sentences.en: Ah yes.
Yeah, I booked somewhere to stay on a trip and the reviews were all really good.
sentences.ko: 응, 여행 가서 묵을 곳을 예약했는데 후기가 다 정말 좋았어.

sentences.en: And then when I checked again, the reviews were all really bad.
sentences.ko: 그런데 다시 확인해 보니까 후기가 다 정말 안 좋은 거야.

sentences.en: Oh no! What were they about?
They said the place was dirty and things were broken.
sentences.ko: 그곳이 더럽고 물건들이 고장 나 있다고 했어.

sentences.en: Oh no. What did you do? Have you been yet?
sentences.ko: 아이고. 그래서 어떻게 했어? 벌써 다녀왔어?

sentences.en: Not yet. No.
So, what did you do?
I wrote to them.
I sent them an email to say I was worried.
And I asked them to assure me that the place would be clean and working properly.
sentences.ko: 그리고 숙소가 깨끗하고 다 제대로 작동할 거라고 확인해 달라고 요청했어.

sentences.en: OK. And did you get a response?
I did, but I really hated the whole process.
sentences.ko: 받았어. 그런데 그 과정 전체가 정말 싫었어.

sentences.en: Oh no! Why?
Because I don't like complaining.
No, neither do I.
I'm not very good at it.
I don't like to make people feel bad.
sentences.ko: 사람들 기분을 상하게 하는 게 싫어.

sentences.en: Even if there is a problem, and I've paid for something and it should be a certain way, but it's not and I'm entitled to complain, I still don't like it.
sentences.ko: 문제가 있어도, 돈을 냈고 원래 어떠해야 하는데 그렇지 않아서 불평할 자격(entitled)이 있는데도, 여전히 싫어.

sentences.en: I just feel...
yeah, I feel embarrassed about it.
Yeah, it's not an easy thing to do, I think.
sentences.ko: 응, 쉬운 일이 아닌 것 같아.

sentences.en: I think I'm getting better with age.
sentences.ko: 나는 나이 들면서 점점 나아지고 있는 것 같아.

sentences.en: I think I'm getting braver.
I had an experience a couple of weeks ago.
Because I am subscribed to a food delivery service, I get a box of food every week, and the last two weeks the delivery has been very late and I'm not happy about it.
sentences.ko: 음식 배달 서비스를 구독하고 있어서 매주 음식 상자를 받는데, 지난 2주 동안 배달이 엄청 늦어서 불만이었어.

sentences.en: And so, I found the courage – found the bravery to call up the customer service and complain.
sentences.ko: 그래서 용기를 내서 고객 서비스에 전화해서 불평했어.

sentences.en: And I was very strong.
And I asked for money – a discount on the next order.
sentences.ko: 보상을 요청했어. 다음 주문 때 할인해 달라고.

sentences.en: Wow, that sounds very well done.
I think when you do complain, sometimes you feel bad about it.
sentences.ko: 불평을 하면 가끔 기분이 안 좋을 때가 있는 것 같아.

sentences.en: But if it works out well, like with you and hopefully with my accommodation...
sentences.ko: 그런데 너처럼, 그리고 바라건대 내 숙소처럼 잘 해결되면...

sentences.en: Yes.
...afterwards you feel really good.
Yes.
Because you did what was right.
Yeah. If you've paid for something, I think you can expect it to be what you paid for.
sentences.ko: 응. 돈을 냈으면 낸 만큼의 것을 기대할 수 있다고 생각해.

sentences.en: So, if it isn't, I think you're allowed to...
you're allowed to complain.
But there is a nice way to do it, isn't there?
sentences.ko: 그런데 좋게 하는 방법이 있잖아, 그렇지?

sentences.en: There is, yeah. Be polite.
Don't be personal.
It's not often...
The person you are complaining to is often not the person responsible for the mistake or whatever.
sentences.ko: 내가 불평하는 상대는 그 실수나 뭐든 간에 책임이 있는 사람이 아닌 경우가 많아.

sentences.en: Yeah.
So, I think if you are respectful and polite but you know what you want.
sentences.ko: 그러니까 존중하고 예의 바르게 하되, 원하는 건 분명히 아는 게 좋은 것 같아.

sentences.en: So Neil, you and I find complaining quite stressful so we don't do it very often.
sentences.ko: 닐, 너랑 나는 불평하는 게 꽤 스트레스라서 자주 안 하잖아.

sentences.en: But do you know anyone that complains all the time?
Oh yeah. Some people seem to love complaining and they complain about things that I would not complain about.
sentences.ko: 아, 알지. 어떤 사람들은 불평하는 걸 좋아하는 것 같고, 나라면 불평하지 않을 일에도 불평해.

sentences.en: Yeah, I've been in restaurants with groups of people where there's been someone that has complained about something that is really embarrassing, and you just think this is not a real, big issue.
sentences.ko: 응, 여러 사람이랑 레스토랑에 갔는데 누가 정말 민망한 걸로 불평한 적이 있어. 이건 진짜 큰 문제가 아닌데 싶었지.

sentences.en: Has that ever happened to you?
Yeah, the same thing.
I've been having a meal with some friends and one of the people I was with – he used to be a waiter, and he had a very clear idea about how waiters should behave.
sentences.ko: 친구들이랑 밥을 먹고 있었는데, 같이 있던 사람 중 하나가 예전에 웨이터였어. 그래서 웨이터가 어떻게 행동해야 하는지에 대한 생각이 아주 확고했어.

sentences.en: And he didn't like something and he complained about it, and nobody else really understood what he was talking about or why he was complaining.
sentences.ko: 그런데 뭔가 마음에 안 드는 게 있어서 불평했는데, 다른 사람들은 그가 무슨 말을 하는 건지, 왜 불평하는 건지 아무도 이해를 못 했어.

sentences.en: And it was embarrassing.
Did he complain to the waiter?
Yeah, but so everyone could hear.
sentences.ko: 응, 그런데 모두가 들을 수 있게.

sentences.en: Oh no. And how did the waiter respond?
I don't think he liked it very much.
Well, I used to work in restaurants.
I've also worked in customer service, but in restaurants, if people have a reason to complain, of course I'm going to try to fix it.
sentences.ko: 고객 서비스 일도 했는데, 레스토랑에서 손님이 불평할 이유가 있으면 당연히 해결하려고 노력해.

sentences.en: But it also depends how they say it.
If they're very rude, as a waitress you don't really want to help them.
sentences.ko: 아주 무례하면 웨이트리스로서 별로 도와주고 싶지 않아.

sentences.en: But if they're polite and they have a reason to complain, of course I'll try to fix their problems.
sentences.ko: 그런데 예의 바르고 불평할 이유가 있으면, 당연히 문제를 해결하려고 노력하지.

sentences.en: OK. Neil, it's time to recap the vocabulary we used in this conversation.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 닐, 이번 대화에서 쓴 어휘를 복습할 시간이야.

sentences.en: We used the verb 'complain', which is when you say something is wrong or not good enough.
sentences.ko: 'complain'이라는 동사를 썼는데, 뭔가 잘못됐거나 충분히 좋지 않다고 말하는 거야.

sentences.en: And we also heard the noun 'complaint'.
We did. And you 'make a complaint', don't you?
sentences.ko: 맞아. 그리고 'make a complaint'라고 하지, 그렇지?

sentences.en: Yes. We also heard 'discount', which is when you don't pay the full price of something.
sentences.ko: 응. 'discount'도 나왔는데, 정가를 다 내지 않는 걸 말해.

sentences.en: You also said that people are 'entitled' to something, and it means that that is something they should get if they paid for it.
sentences.ko: 너는 사람들이 무언가에 'entitled'되어 있다고도 했는데, 돈을 냈다면 마땅히 받아야 하는 거라는 뜻이야.

sentences.en: And Neil, you said you were worried about the 'reviews' of the accommodation for your trip, which is when people write what they think about the place.
sentences.ko: 그리고 닐, 너는 여행 숙소의 'reviews'가 걱정됐다고 했지. 사람들이 그곳에 대해 어떻게 생각하는지 쓴 글이야.

sentences.en: That's it then, Georgie, isn't it?
But join us again, another time for more Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: 다음에도 Real Easy English로 함께해 주세요.

sentences.en: Don't forget, there's a free worksheet on the website.
sentences.ko: 웹사이트에 무료 워크시트가 있다는 거 잊지 마세요.

sentences.en: Goodbye for now.
Goodbye.
